I understand the bug now. Let me analyze the `fio_keyword_replace` function:

The bug is in the `memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1)` line. After `opt += strlen(kw->word) + olen`, the `opt` pointer points past the keyword. Then `memcpy` copies `opt - o_org - 1` bytes from `opt`. But `opt - o_org - 1` = `strlen(kw->word) + olen - 1`. This copies bytes from `opt` (which is after the keyword) but the length is based on the position before the keyword. This can cause a heap-buffer-overflow read when the keyword is at the end of the string.
